brief: UniCredit's daily note argues that Fed rate hikes have historically hurt equities only briefly. After the first hike of a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 typically fell over the following one to three months, but was higher six months later in five of seven historical episodes since 1988, and averaged roughly 8% one year out; the two exceptions, 1994 and 2022, occurred when policy turned more restrictive than markets expected. Against this backdrop, and with a 25bp ECB hike expected today, UniCredit has revised its Fed forecast to two 25bp hikes, in September and December, citing resilient growth, a labor market near full employment, slower disinflation, accommodative financial conditions, and inflation pressure from the Iran conflict. The bank's view: a more hawkish Fed does not conflict with a constructive equity stance, because the growth, labor and earnings backdrop that justified the forecast remains intact; higher rates may instead broaden market leadership beyond long-duration growth stocks rather than derail the broader equity story.
